answer: A concrete anti-sybil rule is two-step enrollment: a unique stylus-captured signature, like a modern quill stroke of a one-time phrase, plus a time-locked bond. The phrase is revealed only when a 15-minute ledge opens on the calendar, so farms cannot pre-record or reuse a single signing session. The bond equals ten times the last epoch's median attestation payout and is burned if another account shows a near-duplicate stroke or the same device attestation. Creating 100 sybils costs 100 live sessions in distinct windows and 100 locked bonds; a gale of scripted keys arrives with neither.
